text:
Erin: Heads-up: enterprise asked for robust 'multi-invoke' tool-calling: parallel calls, deterministic merge, per-tool retries/timeouts. Need MVP scope.

Sam: +1. Clarify 'deterministic' — strict ordering or stable merge? :thinking_face: 

Marta: From the customer call: they need a reproducible merge for downstream indexing. Ordering isn't strict, but merge must be stable given the same inputs and retry outcomes.

Ian: Tradeoffs: parallel fanout reduces latency but increases cost (N calls per request), complicates retry semantics, and makes KV-cache reuse harder.

Erin: Proposed MVP (high level):
- Unordered parallel fanout with a reproducible 'stable' merge (sort by tool id + response checksum).
- Per-tool timeout and max-retries config (client-specified, capped by global safety limits).
- If a tool fails after retries, include an explicit error placeholder in merged output and surface per-tool status.

Sam: Also expose a sequential fallback mode in the API so customers can opt out of parallelism for cost/determinism reasons.

Alice: SDK ergonomics idea — per-invoke options. Example:
invokes = [ {"tool": "search", "timeout_ms": 500, "retries": 1}, {"tool": "extract", "timeout_ms": 2000, "retries": 0} ]
mode = "parallel"  # or "sequential"
merge = "stable"  # options: stable | first-success | pass_through

Marta: Define merge=stable: sort by tool name, then by deterministic hash of each response payload, then concatenate. Guarantees stable order without enforcing causal ordering.

Ian: Edge case: retries may return different payloads. Stable-sort stays deterministic but not idempotent across different responses. Need a response_version and request-idempotency guidance.

Kevin: QA launch criteria: deterministic merge unit tests (including flaky tool stubs), latency regression checks for fanout sizes (1, 3, 5 tools), and cost-per-call telemetry.

Erin: Draft launch criteria: API spec + SDK documented; E2E canary with 2 customers; Perf SLO: p95 end-to-end latency for 3-tool parallel under 800ms on baseline infra; Observability: per-tool timing, retry counts, cost attribution in Console; Security: parallel payloads must respect data routing/policies.

Sam: Prioritization question: runtime merge vs client-side merge. Runtime merge = higher product value but more eng work.

Erin: Leaning runtime merge (stable by default) because customers asked for server-side deterministic outputs for indexing. Provide pass_through=true so clients can merge themselves.

Alice: SDK representation: merged output includes __tool_metadata per item with fields: tool, status, latency_ms, attempts. Will include in SDK PR.

Marta: Partial success schema suggestion: each merged item is either {ok: true, tool: "x", result: {...}} or {ok: false, tool: "x", error: "timeout"}. Explicit and easy for downstream indexing.

Ian: Retry policy: support two modes — idempotent_only (default) and best_effort. Default idempotent_only. Also expose max_total_attempts global cap.

Erin: Can we ship MVP with: parallel runtime merge (stable), per-tool timeout/retry, default idempotent-only retries, sequential fallback, and the SDK representation above? Who's blocking what?

Kevin: QA will cover harness once API contract is final. Need feature flag for canary rollout.

Sam: Rough eng estimate: ~8w (4w infra + 2w runtime merge + 1w SDK + 1w docs/qa). Can compress by scoping merge to flat arrays of tool results.

Erin: Action items: Sam: eng spec with failure modes + safety caps (due EOD Fri); Marta: draft API JSON schema and examples (due Tue); Alice: SDK stub PR for JS/Python (due Wed); Kevin: test plan skeleton (due Wed); Erin: find 2 canary customers and start contract review.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature-flag scaffolding created by sam (build/1234) :rocket:

Alice: noted — I'll start the SDK PR with merge: "stable" default and include __tool_metadata.

Marta: sample merged response for docs: { "merged": [ {"ok": true,  "tool": "search",    "result": {...}, "__tool_metadata": {"latency_ms": 120, "attempts": 1}}, {"ok": false, "tool": "summarize", "error": "timeout", "__tool_metadata": {"latency_ms": 2000, "attempts": 3}} ] }

Erin: Anyone object to this scope? If not I'll lock the MVP decisions and Sam will post the eng-spec thread.

Sam: no objections.

Kevin: QA has no objections, will prep flaky-tool harness.

Marta: no objections, adding docs checklist to my task.

Erin: Locking MVP. Thanks team :tada:
